court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before M.M. Sundresh and Teekaa Raman, JJ.)
respondents: State of Tamil Nadu, Rep. by the Secretary to Government and Others .…. Respondents.
advocates: For Respondents: Mr. R. Prathap Kumar, Additional Public Prosecutor
judgment_text:
Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying to issue a Writ of Habeas Corpus, directing the respondent to grant 30 days ordinary leave to petitioner's father Mr. Sekar @ Gunasekar, aged 53 years, Son of Sachidanandham, Life Convict, Ct. No. 21210, now confined in Central Prison, Vellore.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

M.M. Sundresh, J.:— The petitioner is the daughter of the convict, who has been under incarceration for having committed offence under Section 302 IPC. Ordinary Leave has been sought for on the premise that the convict's wife requires surgery.

2. Heard both sides.

3. Inasmuch as the conduct of surgery is not in dispute coupled with the fact that the conduct of the convict is good, we are inclined to grant two weeks ordinary leave to the convict.

4. Accordingly, we direct the respondents to grant ordinary leave to the convict for two weeks subject to the usual conditions that can be imposed by the respondents. The convict shall be released from the prison at 10.00 a.m. on 13.09.2019 and that the convict shall return back to the prison at 05.00 p.m. on 28.09.2019. We make it clear that the day on which the convict is released from the prison and the day on which he is readmitted will have to be excluded from the leave.

5. In the result, the Habeas Corpus Petition is disposed of with the above directions.

6. List this matter on 30.09.2019 for reporting compliance.
